messages:
Alicia (docs): I opened a PR to add an on-call runbook + quickstart examples for Dedicated capacity provisioning. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4823 — want autoscale examples, terraform snippet, and a short SLA blurb in the intro.
Ben (infra): Looking. Quick heads-up — we should call out preemptible/spot node behavior separately. Customers keep asking about eviction rules.
Sam (eng-runtime): I can review the autoscale policy examples. Do we want to recommend target_cpu=60 (more stable) or 50? Our perf tests preferred 60 for steady latency.
Alicia (docs): Good point. I left a TODO in the PR to pick a default. If Sam prefers 60 I can update. Also added a placeholder for 'canary fallback' wording for rollouts.
Rahul (legal): Please avoid 'guaranteed' in the public docs. For SLAs use 'SLA-backed (for Dedicated contracts)' vs 'best-effort' for hosted. I'll add suggested phrasing after quick review.
Maria (solutions): I can add a migration note for customers moving from shared-hosted to Dedicated. Need a terraform snippet and an SDK example for Node + Python. Will anyone pair on var names?
Alicia (docs): I added a terraform example under the PR:
```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_reservation" "prod-pool" {
  region = "us-west-2"
  gpu_type = "a10g"
  count = 4
  autoscale {
    min = 2
    max = 8
    target_cpu = 60
  }
}
```
Can someone sanity-check the attribute names?
Ben (infra): terraform looks fine; rename gpu_type -> accelerator to match the provider schema. Also add `eviction_strategy = "none"` for non-spot pools to be explicit.
doc-bot: link-checker: broken link found -> /dedicated/old-autoscale (in PR file docs/dedicated/ops.md line 42).
Alicia (docs): thanks doc-bot — will remove that legacy anchor.
Sam (eng-runtime): On autoscale docs: add note about burst capacity config (burst_capacity: true) and how it interacts with SLA. If burst is used, latency SLOs still rely on available reserved GPUs.
Rahul (legal): For the SLA blurb, propose: "Dedicated reservations include an uptime SLA for reserved capacity; fallback to compatible model variants may occur during maintenance windows." I'll drop exact language in the PR comments.
Maria (solutions): SDK snippet for Node I drafted — can someone verify method names: 
```js
const rw = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new rw.Client({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
await client.dedicated.createReservation({ region: 'us-west-2', accelerator: 'a10g', count: 4 });
```
Does `client.dedicated.createReservation` look correct?
Ben (infra): API call naming is okay for docs; in the SDK we call it `client.reservations.create` but we can accept the higher-level phrasing in quickstart. Maybe add a note mapping quickstart -> SDK surface.
Alicia (docs): I'll add a small mapping table: quickstart sample vs canonical SDK call. Also adding a short troubleshooting checklist for oncall:
- check capacity dashboard
- check model routing policy (fallback to smaller variant)
- escalate to infra if eviction_rate > 0.1%
- roll back recent config changes
Sam (eng-runtime): Add a sample log grep for eviction detection: `grep -i "evicted" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log` and the query for Console metrics: `evictions{pool="prod-pool"}`.
Alicia (docs): Good. One more: doc-bot flagged a missing internal link to the SLO matrix. I'll add it but keep it behind the staff doc flag.
Rahul (legal): Confirming I removed any 'guarantee' wording and replaced with the SLA note.
Ben (infra): I pushed a small PR commit to fix the terraform var name and the broken link.
Maria (solutions): I updated the migration snippet to include `provider = "gcp"` example and a short note about networking differences for VPC private deployments.
Alicia (docs): Amazing — I think we're close. I'll merge once the link-check is clean and Rahul OKs the SLA sentence. After merge, I'll open a follow-up to add a short oncall playbook (runbook steps with pager links). :shipit:
